# Market Resilience Amid Multiple Challenges - The Friday Market Wrap!

First listed: 2025-06-13 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Market Resilience Amid Multiple Challenges - The Friday Market Wrap!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V-tAUh_cUhs) - 2025-06-13
- [Substack: Market Resilience Amid Multiple Challenges - The Friday Market Wrap!](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/market-resilience-amid-multiple-challenges-201) - 2025-06-14

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

The wrap connects trade data, rare-earth leverage, media restructuring and AI earnings, then gives a substantive account of how Eisman tracked the mortgage crisis. He emphasizes loan-vintage deterioration, incentives and the danger of mistaking limited data for evidence of safety. His claim that there is literally no private-credit quality data is too broad.

The loan-level research framework is stronger than the categorical statements around it. Public BDC disclosures already offered some private-credit evidence, even though coverage was incomplete. The Apple AI dismissal also ignores announced features while leaving competitive leadership unsettled.

### 001. The reported 35% fall in China-to-US exports confirms Fuller earlier shipping warning, with further weakness likely absent a deal.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | forecast | major

[Source at 0:54-1:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V-tAUh_cUhs&t=54s) | Stance: endorsed guest explanation | Horizon: not stated

<a id="youtube-V-tAUh_cUhs-c010"></a>
### 010. Rapid early delinquency in recent mortgage vintages was a useful warning that pre-crisis credit quality was deteriorating.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 7:24-8:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V-tAUh_cUhs&t=444s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The crisis inquiry supports deterioration in underwriting and mortgage performance. His personal monthly research routine is a recollection, not an independently audited trading record.

Assessment test: Compare vintages at equal months of seasoning and follow delinquency-to-loss transitions.

- [Financial Crisis Inquiry Report](https://fcic-static.law.stanford.edu/cdn_media/fcic-reports/fcic_final_report_full.pdf) (2011-01-27): The inquiry documents deteriorating mortgage vintages, weak underwriting, leverage, compensation incentives and institutional risk-management failures.

<a id="youtube-V-tAUh_cUhs-c011"></a>
### 011. There is literally no private-credit quality data, only volume data.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 8:48-9:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V-tAUh_cUhs&t=528s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Ares Capital had already published non-accruals, credit grades and realized losses. Data coverage was incomplete, but zero is false for private lending as broadly discussed.

Qualification: This correction does not imply that public BDC data describe all private credit or eliminate valuation opacity.

Assessment test: Inspect public BDC filings and distinguish observed portfolios from the unreported fund universe.

- [Ares Capital Q1 2025 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1287750/000128775025000018/arccq1-2025exhibit991.htm) (2025-04-29): The public direct-lender release disclosed non-accrual balances, portfolio credit grades and realized losses before this episode. It does not provide complete data for all private-credit funds.

## Framework and tools

- Follow vintage delinquency progression to test a credit thesis.
- Do not confuse loan growth with loan quality.
- Analyze incentives rather than assuming bad outcomes come only from stupidity.
- Look for dependence that changes bargaining power.
- Treat corporate restructuring as a proposal whose cash economics still need testing.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Export value versus shipping orders
- Rare-earth concentration
- Streaming margins and resource scale
- Cloud revenue and EPS forecasts
- Thirty-, sixty- and ninety-day delinquencies
- Real-estate-owned balances, losses and securitization vintages
- Private-credit non-accruals and portfolio marks

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.
- The claimed match between Fuller forecast and realized exports may compare shipping order/volume data with customs dollar values; it is not automatically an exact forecasting success.
- Oracle quarter ended May 31; $6.03 annual adjusted EPS is garbled in captions.
- Mailbag identity and biographical details are omitted because they are not material investment claims.
